# Exact-head refresh campaign, 2026-09-08

## Causal improvement campaign

The `perf/pr-improve-20260908` successor keeps the same pinned main and acceptance tolerances. New source fixes receive new exact candidate pins. Shared microbenchmarks now capture CLR MethodJittingStarted events alongside runtime boundary samples to identify residual compilation activity; this instrumentation applies identically to A1/B/A2. Its observer cost remains in the measured process. No compilation event or latency sample is excluded, and these diagnostic runs cannot substitute for missing loaded acceptance evidence. Compare each result with the preceding exact-head refresh and preserve both.

The outbox suite retains its preceding four-case fixture, twenty-second direct warmup, thirty BDN warmups, twenty-five measured samples, tiered compilation disabled, and stricter 1% timing/2% control drift limits. It adds the same JIT attribution logger. All listener modes remain measured, including the enabled baseline's known lack of instruments. Duration tracking moved outside the disabled product path; that causal candidate requires fresh measurement of enabled and disabled modes.

The dispatch refresh runner exposed two physical cores with two hardware threads each. Fixed logical CPU numbers did not ensure physical isolation between the consumer and upstream processes. The next experiment reads Linux CPU/core/socket topology, gives the consumer every available hardware thread of the last physical core, and confines the baseline producer and Kafka to the other core(s). It rejects machines exposing fewer than two physical cores and records the complete mapping. Workloads, rates, durations, runtime settings, raw latency retention and acceptance tolerances remain unchanged. This addresses resource interference; it does not waive latency losses, startup transitions or missing loaded shutdown coverage.

This task-scoped branch must not be merged. Baseline is `693a02e52b120ccd33ba1328843b0a052ec6766e`, containing #3143 and #3144. Candidate SHAs are explicit workflow inputs and must contain the baseline. Preserve each PR's prior evidence; new pins supersede old-head acceptance, not historical observations.

Shared microbenchmark fixtures come unchanged from `perf/ubuntu-aba-20260907`. The driver now requests fifty one-second workload warmups and verifies at least twenty elapsed workload seconds per case. It retains twenty-five actual iterations, every outlier, MemoryDiagnoser output, and runtime samples at workload boundaries. Runtime sampling is reused from the pool harness. Release/net10.0, InProcessEmit, tiered compilation disabled, and CPU affinity are identical across A1/B/A2. Both products build and every fixture validates before timing. This isolates costs; it does not supply end-to-end acceptance.

Pool rent/return uses the unchanged fixture from `perf/pool-reset-count-3141`, with explicit product inputs. Both products run the same fixture, twenty elapsed seconds of direct workload, thirty one-second BDN warmups, twenty-five actual iterations, and tiered compilation/PGO enabled. Identity/count checks and an exact allocation probe accompany MemoryDiagnoser. Reset failure and loaded recovery remain separate requirements.

Predeclare microbenchmark mean-time loss tolerance 3% against each control, maximum control drift 5%, and no candidate per-message allocation increase. Require 0 B on per-message hot paths; distinguish per-batch and cold-path allocation. Report absolute A1/B/A2, both deltas, control drift, sample counts and confidence bounds. A confirmed loss is REGRESSION. Missing protected metrics, unresolved startup, noisy controls, invalid fixtures or insufficient precision are INCONCLUSIVE. No script turns workflow success into a performance PASS.

Producer stress uses each rebased product's merged workflow unchanged: producer-1b, cheap, five minutes per phase, 1,000-byte messages, 180-second workload warmup, profiling off. Existing comparator limits and startup assessment stay unchanged. Each PR runs A1/B/A2 on one ubuntu-latest VM. Pool diagnostics supplement that loaded evidence.

Administrative direct-call probes reuse the existing PR-specific fixture and accounting validators. Every configuration has 180 seconds of elapsed workload warmup and 60 measured seconds, tiered compilation/PGO enabled, workstation GC, sequential closed-loop completed calls. This increases the earlier 120-second warmup uniformly; it does not assume startup has ended. Existing calls run A1/B/A2 before candidate-only new API characterization. Both exact products and every selected configuration validate before measurement. There is no incremental optimization claim. Raw exact-tick histograms, maxima, one-second CPU/allocation/JIT/thread-pool/GC/heap/RSS samples, sources and loaded binaries are retained. Administrative allocations are per completed call, not per-message hot-path allocations. The existing comparator limits remain 3% throughput/CPU, 5% p50/p99/max, 1 B/call allocation, with controls assessed separately. Cached transport does not cover real broker behavior; overall acceptance remains INCONCLUSIVE until that scope and startup/uncertainty are resolved. These bounded runs do not establish long-term stability.

The dispatch fixture from `pr-3117-hosted-evidence` now initializes and verifies zero committed offsets before any warmup or producer offers. Run 34218648542 completed all 12,050,000 baseline records but failed its first offset commit with NotCoordinator as the broker initialized __consumer_offsets at shutdown. Setup retries only retriable Kafka errors, at most five attempts; a failed preflight still aborts. No measured error is caught or suppressed. Final commit/drain assertions, all loads, warmup durations, timing boundaries and tolerances stay unchanged. The failed run is preserved and never treated as a candidate regression or complete A1/B/A2. The correction applies identically to every baseline, candidate and smoke process.
